title: Routing: round robin, least loaded, or by prefix
design_ref: Routing: prefix-aware routing and the endpoint picker
purpose: Put the same four replicas behind three routing policies and measure the prefix-cache hit rate the servers report, the wait for the first token of code requests, and goodput; the router is a small stand-in for the gateway's endpoint picker and says so.

steps.output:
policy    cache hit rate   code TTFT p50 at 0.9/GPU   capacity req/s/GPU   goodput tok/s/GPU
rr                25%               1.19 s             0.64             71.2
least             27%               1.19 s             0.67             72.0
prefix            53%               0.32 s             0.75             71.8

checks.description: policy rr: four replicas and the router start
policy least: four replicas and the router start
policy prefix: four replicas and the router start
the prefix-aware policy gets a higher prefix-cache hit rate from the same servers than round robin does
checks.because: Hit rate 53% against 25%. Round robin sends each repository's requests to all four servers, so each server must cache all 48 repositories (about 57,000 tokens) in room for about 20,000; the prefix policy sends a repository to the server that already holds it, so each holds about a quarter.

checks.description: the prefix policy sends requests to servers that already had the prefix (the router counts the matches it made)
checks.because: The router's own counter of prefix matches: 1574 of 1635 requests.

checks.description: the prefix policy does not pile everything on one replica: the busiest replica takes less than 1.6 times the average
checks.because: Busiest replica 1.41 times the mean. The router skips a replica that is well above the average load, so one popular repository cannot saturate one server.

notes: Best policy by capacity then goodput: prefix. Round robin and least-loaded ignore what is cached; the gap between them and the prefix policy is the part of the traffic that repeats.

This router is 150 lines of Python in this repository. The Gateway API Inference Extension implements the same two ideas (load-aware and prefix-aware picking) as a component of the gateway; it is not installed here, so what was measured is the policy and not that product.
